summary: Elizabeth De Michelis is an indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned a master's at SOAS (~1993–1995) and a PhD at Cambridge (~1997–2001), where she was director in 2000, and held a post at Oxford's theology faculty.

Elizabeth English is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999, studying under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson and teacher Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar. She held posts at the Fitzwilliam Museum (1992), the British Museum (curator, 1993), and the University of Oxford (~2016).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury (~1989–1994) and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Y. Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1988–1993) and held a post at the University of Birmingham (~2017).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978) and held posts at the University of Washington (~1982–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).
Elizabeth Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 2011. She later taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto (attested 2020).

Elizabeth Napper is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Ngawang Wangyal. She later served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. In 2021, she served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester.

Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar in archaeology and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006), supervised by Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, with co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She held academic posts at Leiden University (attested 2003, 2018) and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).

Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (1998). He was supervised by George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass, and studied under traditional teacher P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1978–1979).

Elliot Sperling (1951–2017) was a historian and Tibetologist who earned his M.A. and Ph.D. at Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Lynn Struve. He was associate professor at Indiana (1987–2015) and held posts at Harvard and Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, where she was associate professor (attested 1989).
Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He served as a pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library, an editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926), and held posts at Sanskrit Pathashala (attested 1937) and Baroda (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita is an archaeology and history scholar. She studied under John C. Huntington at Ohio State University (MA ~1998–2001), serving as a graduate assistant, after working as a lecturer for the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education (1994–1996).
Emil Krebs (1867–1930) was a linguist and sinologist. He studied at the University of Breslau in 1887 and at the University of Berlin (~1887–1890) under Wilhelm Grube.

Emil Rödiger (1801–1874) was a linguist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Halle (Dr. phil. 1826), he served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Halle (1830–1860) and the University of Berlin (1860).

Emil Sieg (1866–1951) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at Berlin (1891) under Albrecht Weber, Franz Kielhorn, and Ernst Kuhn. He held chairs at Kiel University (1909; 1918–1919) and the University of Göttingen (from 1920).
